name: Kong Gateway
tagline: Declarative API gateway: routes, plugins and upstreams in front of every service.

howItWorks.title: What it is and where it sits
howItWorks.body:
Kong Gateway is an API gateway built on NGINX and OpenResty, extended with Lua plugins.
It works at L7: routes match Host, path, method and headers.
Stream routes can proxy raw TCP and TLS at L4.
It sits in the Edge layer: behind a load balancer, in front of services.

howItWorks.title: Entities
howItWorks.body:
A Service describes one upstream: protocol, host, port and path.
A Route matches requests by host, path, method or header and points to a Service.
A Plugin attaches behaviour at global, Service, Route or Consumer scope.
A Consumer identifies a client or app for credentials and per-client limits.
An Upstream with Targets adds balancing and active or passive health checks.

howItWorks.title: Request phases
howItWorks.body:
Kong listens on 8000 for HTTP and 8443 for HTTPS by default.
The router picks the best-matching Route; Route and Service plugins are then resolved.
The access phase runs authentication, then rate limiting, by plugin priority.
The balancer picks a healthy Target and reuses upstream keepalive connections.
Header and body filters shape the response; log plugins ship it after completion.

howItWorks.title: Config modes
howItWorks.body:
DB-backed mode stores entities in PostgreSQL; the Admin API changes them live.
DB-less mode loads one declarative file and needs no database.
Hybrid mode pushes config from a control plane to data planes.
Data planes keep serving from cached config if the control plane drops.
Check each plugin supports DB-less before choosing that mode.

howItWorks.title: Config as code with decK
howItWorks.body:
Git holds kong.yaml as the source of truth.
deck gateway diff previews changes; deck gateway sync applies them.
deck gateway dump exports a live gateway into a file.
Tags and workspaces split files per team.

howItWorks.title: Security
howItWorks.body:
Authenticate with key-auth, basic-auth, jwt, oauth2 or, in Enterprise, openid-connect.
The jwt plugin can validate tokens issued by an external identity provider.
Bind the Admin API to localhost; remote access needs RBAC or mTLS in front.
Use rate-limiting, ip-restriction and request-size-limiting to protect upstreams.
Upstream TLS verification is configured per Service with ca_certificates and tls_verify.

howItWorks.title: Observability
howItWorks.body:
The prometheus plugin exposes request counts, latency and bandwidth per Service and Route.
The status endpoint reports database reachability and connection counters.
Log plugins ship access logs to files, HTTP endpoints or syslog.
OpenTelemetry tracing is available through a plugin.
Alert on 5xx rate, upstream latency p95 and failed health checks.

howItWorks.title: Failure modes and troubleshooting
howItWorks.body:
404 with no Route matched: check host, path, method and strip_path on the Route.
502 or 503 means the upstream refused, or no healthy Target is left.
401 and 403 come from auth plugins; test with the expected header or key.
Rate limiting with policy local counts per node, so limits multiply with node count.
Read the error log first; raise log_level to debug only briefly.

howItWorks.title: Connecting to its neighbours
howItWorks.body:
In front (Users): DNS points at a load balancer or VIP that forwards to the Kong listener.
Behind, on VMs (Infrastructure): Services point at app hosts; Upstreams and Targets add balancing and health checks.
Behind, on Kubernetes (Platform): Kong Ingress Controller reads Ingress or Gateway API resources and configures Kong.
Expose the Kong proxy Service as LoadBalancer (cloud or MetalLB) or NodePort behind your own balancer.
Standalone Kong outside the cluster points Services at NodePort or LoadBalancer addresses, not ClusterIP.
Identity: the jwt or openid-connect plugin validates tokens from an identity provider such as Keycloak.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
NGINX or HAProxy: choose them when you only need routing and TLS, with no plugin ecosystem.
Envoy-based gateways (Envoy Gateway, Emissary): choose them for xDS-driven config and Gateway API.
Traefik: choose it for simple auto-discovery in container setups.
Apache APISIX: choose it for a similar plugin gateway with etcd-backed config.
Cloud API gateways (AWS API Gateway, Azure APIM): choose them when the provider should host the gateway.

flow: The client opens TLS to the Kong listener on 8443, usually via a balancer.
The router matches a Route by host, path and method.
The plugin chain for the Route, Service and Consumer is resolved.
The access phase runs authentication, then rate limiting.
The balancer picks a healthy Target and reuses a keepalive connection.
Targets can be VM APIs or Kubernetes Services and pods.
The response returns through header and body filters; logs and metrics ship.

deploy.summary: On-prem edge: hardened host, firewall, Kong with PostgreSQL, a decK workflow, then Kubernetes.
prerequisites: Linux VM with Docker Engine 24+ and Compose
DNS zone you control and a free VIP or address

steps.title: SSH key and sshd hardening
steps.code:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "ops@edge"
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub ops@EDGE_HOST
sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-hardening.conf <<'EOF'
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
AllowUsers ops
EOF
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
steps.note: Replace ops and EDGE_HOST. Keep a second session open until key login works.

steps.title: DNS record and firewall
steps.code:
dig +short api.example.test
sudo ufw default deny incoming
sudo ufw allow from ADMIN_CIDR to any port 22 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow 8000,8443/tcp
sudo ufw enable
sudo ufw status verbose
steps.note: Create the A record first and replace ADMIN_CIDR. Port 8001 stays closed.

steps.title: Compose file with PostgreSQL and Kong
steps.code:
services:
  kong-db:
    image: postgres:16.4
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: kong
      POSTGRES_DB: kong
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${KONG_PG_PASSWORD:?set a password}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-U", "kong"]
      interval: 5s
      retries: 10
    volumes:
      - kong-pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data
  kong-migrations:
    image: kong:3.8.0
    command: kong migrations bootstrap
    environment: &kongenv
      KONG_DATABASE: postgres
      KONG_PG_HOST: kong-db
      KONG_PG_USER: kong
      KONG_PG_PASSWORD: ${KONG_PG_PASSWORD:?set a password}
    depends_on:
      kong-db:
        condition: service_healthy
  kong:
    image: kong:3.8.0
    environment:
      <<: *kongenv
      KONG_PROXY_LISTEN: 0.0.0.0:8000, 0.0.0.0:8443 ssl
      KONG_ADMIN_LISTEN: 0.0.0.0:8001
      KONG_PROXY_ACCESS_LOG: /dev/stdout
      KONG_ADMIN_ACCESS_LOG: /dev/stdout
      KONG_PROXY_ERROR_LOG: /dev/stderr
      KONG_ADMIN_ERROR_LOG: /dev/stderr
    depends_on:
      kong-migrations:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
      - "8443:8443"
      - "127.0.0.1:8001:8001"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "kong", "health"]
      interval: 10s
      retries: 5
volumes:
  kong-pg:
steps.note: Migrations run once, then Kong starts. Change the password; 8001 binds to localhost only.

steps.title: Start the stack and check status
steps.code:
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
curl -s localhost:8001/status | head -c 400
steps.note: /status shows database reachability and connection counters.

steps.title: Declare service, route and plugin
steps.code:
_format_version: "3.0"
services:
  - name: httpbin
    url: http://httpbin.org
    routes:
      - name: httpbin-route
        paths:
          - /anything
        strip_path: false
    plugins:
      - name: rate-limiting
        config:
          minute: 60
          policy: local
steps.note: Save as kong.yaml. Use policy redis for a cluster-wide limit.

steps.title: Diff, review, then sync with decK
steps.code:
export KONG_ADDR=http://127.0.0.1:8001
deck gateway ping --kong-addr "$KONG_ADDR"
deck gateway diff -s kong.yaml --kong-addr "$KONG_ADDR"
deck gateway sync -s kong.yaml --kong-addr "$KONG_ADDR"
deck gateway diff -s kong.yaml --kong-addr "$KONG_ADDR"
steps.note: Sync deletes entities missing from the file, so read the diff first. The last diff should show no changes.

steps.title: Add key authentication
steps.code:
# append to kong.yaml, then diff and sync again
consumers:
  - username: demo-app
    keyauth_credentials:
      - key: CHANGE_ME_LONG_RANDOM
plugins:
  - name: key-auth
    route: httpbin-route
steps.note: Replace the key with a long random value. Then call with the apikey header.

steps.title: Install on Kubernetes with Helm
steps.code:
helm repo add kong https://charts.konghq.com
helm repo update
kubectl create namespace kong
helm install kong kong/kong -n kong \
  --set image.tag=3.8 \
  --set ingressController.enabled=true \
  --set proxy.type=LoadBalancer \
  --set env.database=off
kubectl -n kong rollout status deploy/kong-kong
steps.note: DB-less with the ingress controller. Use proxy.type=NodePort on bare metal without MetalLB. Pin the chart with --version.

verify: curl -s localhost:8001/services lists the declared service
curl -i localhost:8000/anything/get returns 200 with X-RateLimit headers
deck gateway diff -s kong.yaml reports no changes after sync
kubectl -n kong get svc kong-kong-proxy shows the proxy address
pitfalls: deck sync deletes what is missing from the file; always diff first.
A Route matching nothing returns 404; check strip_path, host and path ordering.
Rate limiting with policy local multiplies the limit by node count.
Exposing the Admin API on 8001 gives full control of the gateway.
Run migrations up before rolling nodes; finish only after all nodes upgrade.
DB-less mode: check every plugin supports it before choosing it.
Plugin order is fixed by priority, not by the order you attach them.
keyPoints: Kong matches Routes, runs plugins, then proxies to Services at L7.
Config is entities: Services, Routes, Plugins, Consumers, Upstreams.
decK diffs and syncs a YAML file, so config lives in Git.
Run DB-less, with PostgreSQL, or hybrid; on Kubernetes use the ingress controller.
quickDeploy: Start Kong and PostgreSQL with Docker Compose.
Declare service, route and plugin in kong.yaml.
Run decK diff, review it, then sync.
Bind the Admin API to localhost; add auth plugins.
osiNote: Routes by Host and path at L7; proxies TCP and TLS at L4.
production: Run three or more data-plane nodes behind a VIP or load balancer.
Back up PostgreSQL; roll back by applying the previous Git version of kong.yaml.
Bind the Admin API to localhost and protect it with RBAC or mTLS.
Set per-Service timeouts and retries; use Redis for cluster-wide rate limits.
Alert on 5xx rate, upstream latency p95 and plugin errors from Prometheus.
